data.one_liner: Official low-level client for Stream Video, supporting calls, audio rooms, and live streaming.
data.what_it_does: Provides low-level interfaces, methods, and device APIs for interacting with Stream Video. It manages call states, participants, media devices, and WebRTC connections for video calls and live streaming.
use_when: You want to build custom UI components on top of the Stream Video SDK instead of using the default UI package.
You need low-level control over audio and video streams, call states, and WebRTC configurations.
You are building video calls, audio rooms, or live-streaming applications.
avoid_when: You want ready-to-use UI components, in which case you should use `stream_video_flutter` instead.
You do not use Stream as your backend video/audio infrastructure.
strengths: Official low-level client backed by Stream's global edge network and infrastructure.
Extensive feature set including dynascale resolution switching, screen sharing, picture-in-picture, and call recording.
Robust stream-based state management for call participants and device configurations.
weaknesses: Requires manual UI implementation since it focuses primarily on low-level logic.
License is under the custom Stream License rather than standard open source.
data.setup_notes: Requires an API key from Stream and registering your app. Platform-specific permissions for camera and microphone are needed for Android and iOS.
